content.comment_body: [product_name] [version_no] on I1 / I2 ON signal causes the module to send multiple SMS messages (between 2 and 6), but I expect just one message. Am I missing something?

Hello [user_name], What type of output are you using to set I1/I2 to active? It sounds like there may be a floating or unstable signal, possibly if you're using a relay as a trigger. This can result in one "high" signal causing multiple transitions internally (from 1 to 0 and back repeatedly) when activated, leading to several assignments. The inputs on the [product_name] are not designed to handle floating signals. You will need to use a debounced output, or manually debounce with a capacitor. Hope this helps. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering an issue where a communication module sends multiple SMS messages in response to a single input, when only one message is expected. This seems related to how the hardware processes the input signal, with insufficient debouncing causing repeated triggers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect each input activation to result in only one SMS message being sent by the module.
